headline: Label-efficient representations for microscopy and histopathology image analysis
label: Biomedical Image Representation Learning
summary: Recent work pairs weak transcriptomic labels, semi-supervised learning, and specialized architectures to reduce annotation demands in microscopy.
synthesis: The dominant thread is reducing annotation dependence in biomedical image learning. A weak-supervision framework uses cell-level spatial transcriptomics to generate image-label pairs for histopathology nuclei classification, and a semi-supervised GAN reaches 93% accuracy on Mitocheck with 80 labels per class plus 600 unlabelled images. Architecture-level work addresses specific tasks: MTCurv regresses microtubule curvature maps from noisy fluorescence images using a segmentation-free attention residual U-Net with gradient-aware loss, DeShiftNet offers lightweight deformable-shifted cross-attention for organoid segmentation with Dice 0.961 on the Lung subset, and FiloAnalyzer provides open-source deep learning segmentation of cell filopodia. What is new is the use of non-image auxiliary signals, transcriptomic labels in particular, to supply supervision for image representations. The items are heterogeneous, so this thread is dominant rather than universal.
